## Summary

`_reads._tracker` raises `store_uninitialized` only when the tracker directory is ABSENT
(`src/rebar/_reads.py`, `if not os.path.isdir(tracker)`). A directory that EXISTS but is not a
usable store — no `.git`, or a `.git` with no resolvable HEAD, or one mid-clone — satisfies
`isdir`, so every read returns `[]`. A broken store is indistinguishable from an empty one, the
exact confusion the guard was added to remove. Hit three times: the deployed MCP server served an
empty tracker (marker files, no `.git`); `fathomable-yester-thrip` change 2244 residual; and
`unfit-beneficial-whimbrel` AC3. Full RCA and escalation are in prior comments.

## Constraints

- An existing, empty, INITIALIZED store must still read `[]` — a real contract with an existing
  test. The discriminator cannot be emptiness.
- `.env-id` is ruled out as the predicate (git-ignored, absent right after a valid clone).
- A `.git`-LESS materialized ticket snapshot must READ: `_snapshot.materialize_tickets` checks the
  committed tickets tree out into a `.git`-less `.tickets-tracker/`, and the code-review gate
  agents read it in production. A `.git`+HEAD-only predicate breaks that surface (the escalation
  the operator resolved with Option A).

## Fix (operator-approved Option A — one shared content-based seam)

New stdlib-only leaf `src/rebar/_store/store_usability.py::store_is_usable(tracker)`: usable when
`isdir` AND EITHER (1) `.git` present with a resolvable HEAD (`git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`), OR
(2) it carries the store STRUCTURE — a committed `.store-compat.json` record (survives the snapshot
checkout, present even in a zero-event store), or ≥1 non-dot event dir (legacy fallback, mirrors
`reducer/_api.py` enumeration). `_reads._tracker` calls `store_is_usable` directly; the write guard
`event_prepare._ensure_initialized` calls `store_is_writable` = `store_is_usable` AND `.git` present
(the write's inherent precondition — it commits events). Both flow through the ONE shared usability
predicate — no mode flag, no second path — so read and write cannot diverge on what an initialized
store is, while a `.git`-less read-only snapshot stays READABLE but correctly non-writable. Clause 2
keeps the `.git`-less snapshot readable while the
marker-file-only production incident still RAISES. Zero events + committed marker is VALID (reads
`[]`); the predicate is never keyed on emptiness.

The HEAD probe reuses the store's bounded runner `gitutil.run_git_bounded` (folds `TimeoutExpired`
to rc 124), so no unbounded git call enters the write path; a missing `git` binary (`OSError`)
propagates as a distinct environment fault, not `store_uninitialized`. The write gate does NOT
loosen: `_ensure_initialized` gates on `store_is_writable(tracker)` = `store_is_usable(tracker)`
AND `.git` present. It shares the usability predicate (so read and write agree on what an
initialized store IS) and then adds the write's inherent precondition — a write COMMITS events, so
it needs a real `.git` repository. This preserves the original `.git`-requiring write gate exactly:
a `.git`-less STRUCTURE-only snapshot is READABLE but NOT writable, and a mid-clone (`.git`, no
HEAD, no structure) is rejected by `store_is_usable` itself. One usability seam, no bypass flag.

The sole `store_uninitialized` consumer, the read-only audit web index
(`audit.server._audited_tickets`), still degrades a broken store to an empty page (must not 500)
but now LOGS a warning and its docstring no longer claims such a store is never blanked — behavior
unchanged; that promise held only while broken stores read `[]`. Caller sweep re-verified against
the NEW predicate: all 7 `_tracker` entry points and the `.git`-less snapshot path behave
correctly. Files: `store_usability.py` (new), `_reads.py`, `event_prepare.py`, `audit/server.py`,
`tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] READ: a dir with marker files only (no `.git`/`.store-compat.json`/event dirs) raises
      `store_uninitialized`, not `[]` — the production incident.
- [x] READ: a mid-clone store (`.git` present, HEAD unresolvable, no structure) raises
      `store_uninitialized`.
- [x] READ: an existing empty INITIALIZED store (`.git`+HEAD) still reads `[]` (contract test
      unchanged).
- [x] READ: a valid clone with resolvable HEAD but no `.env-id` still reads (reads differ from
      writes on `.env-id`).
- [x] READ regression: a `.git`-LESS materialized snapshot with committed `.store-compat.json` +
      an event dir READS the ticket, not raises (the gate-agent path).
- [x] READ edge: a `.git`-less snapshot with `.store-compat.json` and ZERO events reads `[]`.
- [x] WRITE: `_ensure_initialized` (via `store_is_writable`) rejects a mid-clone store, rejects a
      `.git`-LESS materialized snapshot (readable but not writable — no repo to commit into), and
      still accepts an initialized one.
- [x] WRITE: every `stage_and_commit` git call incl. the new HEAD probe is timeout-BOUNDED
      (`test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba`).
- [x] PREDICATE: `store_is_usable` is False for absent/no-`.git`/mid-clone/empty-dir and True for
      an initialized store, a HEAD-resolvable clone without `.env-id`, a snapshot, an
      event-dir-only legacy store, and an empty-but-committed snapshot.
- [x] PREDICATE: a missing `git` binary (OSError) PROPAGATES rather than reporting
      `store_uninitialized` (T5b failure-taxonomy).
- [x] AUDIT: `audit.server._audited_tickets` renders empty AND logs a warning for a
      present-but-unusable store.
- [x] Mutation guard: stripping the store-structure clause returns the `.git`-less snapshot read
      to RAISING `store_uninitialized` (defect-seeded, sandboxed).

## Testing

RED→GREEN in `tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py`; run
`python -m pytest tests/unit/test_reads_uninitialized_store.py -q` (all cases above green). Broad
re-verification: `python -m pytest tests/unit tests/interfaces -q -n auto` — the 6 previously-red
snapshot/next-batch/write-timeout tests are green; `make lint` (complexity ratchet
new=0/increased=0) and `make typecheck` pass. The pre-existing sandbox-git failures
(`show-ref`/`ls-tree refs/heads/tickets` → 128) fail identically on clean `origin/main` and are
environmental, not from this change.

Out of approved scope (parity — discovered ticket): CLI read path (`reads_cli.py`) and other
bare-`isdir` read sites → `free-slothful-fennecfox` (be80-8377-4b4c-44f4).
